title: Highlands County School Board, District 1
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school-tax rate, hire the superintendent (where appointed), approve school boundaries, curriculum policy and construction, and set district policies. Nonpartisan.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: James Jonsten
candidates.background: James Jonsten is an ordained minister who served two years as lay pastor at Burnsville Wesleyan Church in Minnesota and has taught children's church since the 1970s. He has owned construction and commercial services businesses and worked as an insurance claims adjuster, sales manager and trainer. He advanced to the November runoff after taking about 31% of the August 2026 primary vote.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

other_issues.title: Campaign themes
other_issues.summary: Jonsten says education is about building a foundation of leadership and accountability and that he would work to keep Highlands County schools financially sound, safe and focused on student growth. He did not respond to the Florida Trib's interview requests, and no detailed policy positions were located.

sources.title: Three candidates vie for Highlands County District 1 school board seat

candidates.name: Kari Pritchett
candidates.occupation: Former educator; classroom teacher, reading coach, staffing specialist and ESE inclusion teacher
candidates.background: Kari Pritchett was born and raised in Highlands County and holds bachelor's and master's degrees from Florida State University. She worked in the district as a classroom teacher, reading coach, staffing specialist and exceptional student education inclusion teacher, and chaired the District School Advisory Council. She led the August 2026 primary with about 41% of the vote.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

other_issues.title: Campaign themes
other_issues.summary: Pritchett describes herself as a 'responsible conservative steward of taxpayer dollars' and campaigns on academic excellence, transparency, accountability and student success. She did not respond to the Florida Trib's interview requests, and no specific positions on the school tax rate, teacher pay, curriculum, safety or vouchers were located.
